content:
alex: Quick sync — we need clear acceptance criteria for networking fallback behavior in private deployments (VPC/on-prem) during upgrades. Customers keep asking what happens if their peering or egress breaks mid-upgrade. I sketched a draft below, please react and add gaps.

priya: +1. High level: fallback must preserve customer data isolation guarantees, not exfiltrate traffic, and provide deterministic rollback points.

mike: Concrete engineering constraints: fallback options we can implement without kube-level rearchitect are: 1) route to a pinned secondary peering, 2) pause/hold requests (serve 503) with retry window, 3) route to hosted proxy (only for customers that opted in).

sophia: Security rules: hosted proxy option requires explicit customer opt-in, end-to-end encryption with customer KMS, and audit logs for every proxied request. No implicit opt-ins.

linda: Field note: many enterprise customers will refuse any hosted egress. We should design a manual-approval fallback path (ops-only) + clear comms for failover windows.

raj: From the customer side, the acceptance criteria also need a simple API/contract: signal states like `networking: degraded`, `fallback: active|pending|blocked`, and reason codes. Customers want deterministic alerts.

alex: Draft acceptance criteria (v0):
- fallback must not enable outbound-to-hosted unless explicitly opted-in by customer (opt-in recorded in tenant config)
- if fallback to hosted is disabled, system must enter a deterministic degraded state and serve stable 503s for write paths within 30s of detection
- if a secondary peering is configured, fallback must switch traffic within 60s and maintain session affinity where possible
- all fallbacks must be recorded in audit log + incident event with trace id
- rollout: gated behind `priv-net-fallback` feature flag and can be enabled per-tenant via Console

mike: Implementation sketch: add a fallback manager that reads tenant policy at request start, pseudocode: ```
if (tenant.policy.fallback.hosted && network.down) route(hosted-proxy)
else if (tenant.policy.fallback.secondary && secondary.available) route(secondary)
else raise(degraded-503)
```
we'll need health probes for peering and a short retry window (30s) to avoid flapping.

priya: Also need test harness: simulated peering blackout + load test to ensure we don't exceed latency SLOs in fallback. Add integration test that asserts no env vars or headers leak customer internal hostnames when proxied.

sophia: Confirming header/host rewrite requirements: hosted proxy must strip internal host headers and inject X-Redwood-Proxy: true header. KMS envelope for payload in transit.

linda: For field readiness: add a customer-facing runbook page with binary choices: [Allow hosted fallback] [Require manual ops approval] and a matrix of risk + estimated downtime.

raj: Can we expose a telemetry dashboard with these metrics: fallback_count, fallback_duration, fallback_reason, tenant_opt_in? Sales and customers will want to query SLA impact.

deploy-bot: deploy status: feature-branch/priv-net-fallback deployed to staging at 2026-03-20T09:12Z - smoke passed (2/3).

alex: Action items we agreed on:
- priya: add integration tests + header-leak checks (due EOW)
- mike: implement fallback manager + health probes + feature flag (due next sprint)
- sophia: spec KMS + audit logging schema (due 3 business days)
- linda/raj: draft customer runbook and opt-in UI copy (due EOW)
- alex: schedule a short launch readout with sales + support after staging validation

mike: one unresolved: how strict is the 60s switch requirement for secondary peering? some peering BGP convergence in on-prem can be longer. maybe make it SLA-configurable per-tenant.

priya: agreed — change to: target 60s, fallback behavior must be configurable with explicit tenant SLA settings. Document expected variability.

sophia: also require retention of fallback audit events for 1 year for enterprise customers (default 90d for others).

linda: customer-facing acceptance checklist (proposal):
- documented opt-in choice in Console
- visible `networking: degraded` state in Console + webhook alerting
- runbook present and acceptable to customer's NetOps
- legal/compliance sign-off if hosted fallback is enabled

alex: OK — I'll iterate this into a minimal acceptance criteria doc and post a PR to the private-deploy runbook. If no objections I'll mark this thread as the canonical source. :thumbsup:

raj: No objections from field. I'll start collecting a couple of customer examples where manual approval is required.

mike: adding note — we need a metric for "requests dropped due to fallback" so we can measure customer impact during rollout.

priya: tagging QA: @qa-team please review when I push tests.

alex: thanks all — next sync if staging shows >95% smoke pass for fallback flows.
